Alerts & Events

Overspeed Profile

📄 Version 1.0 👤 Audience: Technical Support / Installation Team

The platform offers two ways to measure overspeeding on Assets: instantaneous Overspeed events, and retrospective banded measurement via the Overspeed Profile.

1. Introduction

Instantaneously (START of the speeding)When an Asset goes over the speed limit of the road/location, as defined by the speed limit and tolerances set on the Asset. This is an Overspeed event, and triggers on the first data point breaching the threshold, and every time a subsequent infringement occurs.
Retrospectively (BANDS)By measuring the distance and time of an infringement, using the Overspeed Profile, which can be split into bands based on the severity of the speeding. This measures how long the Asset was in each band during a trip/day, etc.

The Overspeed Profile is designed to measure the time and distance of speeding, helping differentiate serial speedsters from a driver occasionally overtaking another vehicle and infringing the speed limit once off. The difference between an overtaking manoeuvre and constant speeding is shown in these speed graph snippets:

Figure 1: an overtaking manoeuvre

Figure 2: constant speeding

The Overspeed Profile can be split into bands, which are User-defined. For ease of understanding, the examples in this article use a reference of Low, Medium, and High bands. Bands can be called anything, with a % value above the speed limit for each. The table below shows two different examples for a 3-tiered Low/Medium/High profile:

BandExample 1Example 2
Low0–5%5–15%
Medium5–10%15–25%
High> 10%> 25%

Each time the Asset moves into a band, the platform starts recording the time and distance. Only once the Asset moves into another band, or below the lowest, is this recorded and displayed as an event.

The event occurs at the end of the speeding, and should not be used to trigger an Alert — by the time the event fires, the speeding is already finished.

The event will look like this:

The speeding event was 60 seconds and 2.16km long. It was in the Low band.

Speeding bands can also be used in the Asset Rating Profile, with the time or distance used as a penalty — e.g. if a driver goes into the High band and stays there for > 10 seconds, they can be penalised accordingly. There are three steps to using Overspeed bands in a Rating Profile:

1Create an Overspeed Profile
2Add the Overspeed Profile to the Asset/s required
3Create or edit the Asset Rating as needed

2. Create an Overspeed Profile

Overspeed Profiles can be created at Client or Vendor level (all Clients will have access to it). Once created, they need to be assigned to the Asset/s to trigger the events.

1Go to Administration
2Choose the Overspeed section under the Profiles folder
3Click the Plus button
4Enter the information in the Wizard
5Click Next, enter the required information on the following screens, until you reach Finish

A summary of the information entered will appear on screen. Make sure it is correct before choosing Finish — otherwise go Back and edit the information.

The Profile created will display a warning that it is not complete, and that bands need to be added:

Adding Bands to the Profile

Edit the Overspeed Profile, then:

1Click Add
2Complete the details in the Overspeed Band box
3Click OK, then Save those changes

In the example below, the band starts at 10% over the speed limit plus 2 km/h. If the speed limit is 60 km/h, the Speeding Event will trigger at 68 km/h.

3. Adding an Overspeed Profile to an Asset or Multiple Assets

Individual Assets

Choose the Asset you would like to add the Overspeed Profile to, open the Events section, and add the Profile.

Please note: you can only add one speeding type to an Asset — a Profile or a % Tolerance. The Speed Tolerance will disappear if the Overspeed Profile is added to the Asset. This means Events will not trigger on any “tolerance” — only the Bands will apply.

Multiple Assets

Choose the Assets (Ctrl-click) you would like to add the Overspeed Profile to, open the Events section, and add the Profile.

Please note: any Overspeed Profile already added to any of the Assets will be overwritten.

4. Create or Edit an Asset Rating

Create an Asset Rating profile as per usual. To add a Band as an Event, follow the steps below.

Choose Action under the Event Filter, down to Overspeed > Band.

Choose the Profile name, and the band in it to add to the Rating profile (in this example, KTT Band Test I Profile and Low band):

You can further refine the Rating Profile by adding the Distance or Duration of the Event, or Speed, above which the penalty will trigger. In this example, we added Duration > 120 seconds:

5. Reporting on Overspeeding Events

Overspeeding Events per Band Profile can be reported in two ways:

Report TypeDetail
Standard ReportsOverspeeding Report — Profile, showing Distance, Duration in each band, Maximum Speed, and Maximum Percentage over the speed limit
Analytic DashboardsThe Overspeed Profile Analytics Report includes the Instances, Distance, and Duration for each band in the Profile. The Trip Analytics Report also applies if all or some of the profile has been used in the Asset Rating profile.
